messages.author: 51fd275225bf6265
messages.subject: inla crashing while running LGCP
parts:
Dear INLA developers,  

Here is a question that puzzled me for a while. I need to call INLA during a lot of iterations. Each time I need to run the LGCP model to estimate the intensity of a point process. Each point process is formed by pooling of a random number of point processes. All points are defined on a one dimensional domain [0, 10]. The problem I met is that, inla will crash after a few loops, showing an error like

sh: line 1: 65486 Segmentation fault: 11  '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac/64bit/inla.run' -b -s -v '/var/folders/n6/55gqgyj55hdd18byj_t3mhc00000gn/T//RtmphGkh4k/filea06f2a22fd86/Model.ini' > /var/folders/n6/55gqgyj55hdd18byj_t3mhc00000gn/T//RtmphGkh4k/filea06f2a22fd86/Logfile.txt
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does help; please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>. 

Both mac and windows machine show similar errors, with slightly different messages. For your reference, I have made an simple example (including data and R script). You can download the example at: 

https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/93496827/question_on_crash.zip

and reproduce the error. Usually the error appears during the first 50 iterations.The method for running LGCP follows the paper Simpson et al. "Going off grid: LGCP". Any suggestions are welcome.  

Thank you,
Hongxiao Zhu

IntegrationWeights = diag(spde1$param.inla$M0)

IntegrationWeights = diag(inla.mesh.fem(mesh1)$c0)

messages.author: 51fd275225bf6265
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: inla crashing while running LGCP
parts:
Dear Finn and Harvard,

Thank you for the suggestions. After some investigations of my own, I found that the way to avoid crashing is to remove the theta parameter in spde, i.e., use:

spde1 = inla.spde2.matern(mesh1, constr=FALSE,
                          B.tau = cbind(log(tau0)),
                          B.kappa = cbind(log(kappa0))) 

Which means, I need to fix theta in the prior to avoid crashing (at least this is my current observation). Also, I have set the kappa0 prior too small (an ideal value should be 1.5), but that is not related to the crashing issue. 

Best,
Hongxiao Zhu

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: inla crashing while running LGCP
parts:
On 15 Jul 2016, at 19:00, Hongxiao Zhu <hxzh...@gmail.com> wrote:
I tried, but I cannot construct a case for you. The error is a segmentation error coded as Segmentation fault 11, which disappears if I rerun the inla line at the place of crashing.

So rerunning the same inla call, with the same input as the call that crashed, _doesn't_ crash. That's very interesting!

Apart from the prior parameter setting, which itself causes problems, there may be an issue with running many inla calls in a loop. I suspect some systems have problems dealing with all the temporary files used for communication between R, inla, and fmesher, but I've never been able to track down the precise reason.

Finn

I doubt whether you are using the same version of INLA (packaged on 2016-05-18) as I do. The older version (INLA  build in 2013 based on R 2.0.3) runs much more stable, but it would still crashes after a few hundreds of iterations.

Best,
Hongxiao

On 7/15/2016 12:11 PM, Finn Lindgren wrote:
It would be helpful if you could construct a case that crashes and send it to us; the case you sent before was random, and did not crash consistently, so impossible to tell whether it crashes consistently for the same reason as on your system.

Finn

On 15 Jul 2016, at 17:07, Hongxiao Zhu <hxzh...@gmail.com> wrote:

Yes, I had crashes for both large (e.g., theta.prior.prec=10) and small setups (e.g., theta.prior.prec=1e-1, or 1e-2). But looks to me that larger precision gives lesser crashes. That lead me to consider removing the theta from the B.tau.

Another phenomenon I observed is that, INLA runs much much faster on my imac than windows machine, (my mac has i7 4GHz processor, my windows is 2.6GHz, but it is at least 5 times faster).

Hongxiao

On 7/15/2016 10:28 AM, Finn Lindgren wrote:
Changing the prior parameter setting consistently removed the crash on my machine. Are you seeing crashes also for large (e.g. > 1) of the prior precision?

Finn

On 15 Jul 2016, at 15:17, Hongxiao Zhu <hxzh...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear Finn and Harvard,

Thank you for the suggestions. After some investigations of my own, I found that the way to avoid crashing is to remove the theta parameter in spde, i.e., use:

spde1 = inla.spde2.matern(mesh1, constr=FALSE,
                          B.tau = cbind(log(tau0)),
                          B.kappa = cbind(log(kappa0))) 

Which means, I need to fix theta in the prior to avoid crashing (at least this is my current observation). Also, I have set the kappa0 prior too small (an ideal value should be 1.5), but that is not related to the crashing issue. 

Best,
Hongxiao Zhu 


On Thursday, July 14, 2016 at 6:21:33 PM UTC-4, Finn Lindgren wrote:
The line
   IntegrationWeights = diag(spde1$param.inla$M0)
should be
   IntegrationWeights = diag(inla.mesh.fem(mesh1)$c0)
but that's unrelated to the crash.

Your test code crashes on my computer on loop 352, but that's not
replicable since the code doesn't actually set a repeatable random
seed.
In any case, running the problem case with verbose=TRUE reveals that
the optimiser ends up in a bad place (see below).  As H suggested,
your theta.prior.prec is far too small to be sensible.
Increasing it to 1e-4 (which is still really extremely small) removes the crash.

Finn
